claims.text: High-temperature annealing enhances the overall wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coatings.
High-temperature annealing refines the microstructure of FeNiCrCoCu coatings.
The annealing-induced microstructural refinement promotes surface segregation of Cr and Cu.
Surface segregation of Cr and Cu enables formation of a stable, adherent nanoscale protective oxide scale during sliding wear.
The protective oxide scale reduces direct metal-to-metal contact and thermal degradation.
The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a relatively coarse microstructure.
The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has minimal surface oxide.
High-temperature annealing enhances Cr and Cu surface segregation through microstructural refinement.
Preferential oxide formation reduces direct contact and minimizes thermal softening of the coating.
Annealed coatings will have a significantly lower wear rate than as-deposited coatings under identical high-temperature conditions.
Annealed coatings will develop a thicker protective oxide scale than as-deposited coatings.
The protective oxide scale on annealed coatings will be more uniform and adherent than that on as-deposited coatings.
The proposed mechanism applies to sliding wear at approximately 600–700°C.
The proposed mechanism may not apply at room temperature or at loads significantly exceeding the coating's design limits.
